title: Strict reduction compatibility of one completed support exchange
statement:
Let $(A,I,d)$ be the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Take schemes $X,U,Y,X',U',Y'$ and arrows $j:X\to U$, $p:U\to Y$, $j':X'\to U'$, $p':U'\to Y'$, $x:X'\to X$, $u:U'\to U$, $y:Y'\to Y$. Both squares are Cartesian, $xj=j'u$ and $up=p'y$, $j,j'$ are quasi-compact open immersions, and $p,p'$ are proper. Use the ambient constructions of [lem-cbc-completed-support-ambient-comparisons]: completed support $\widehat B_f$, strict support $F_f$, strict reduction $\mathcal R_T$, strict pullback $G_g$, reduction comparison $\theta_f$, completed pullback $g_c^*$, its reduction comparison $q_g$, completed exchange $x_f$, and strict proper-then-open exchange $e_f:F_f\mathbin\gg G_y\to G_x\mathbin\gg F_{f'}$. Then the following equality holds in the derived category of strict quotient diagrams, naturally on every ambient derived input:
$$
(\mathcal R_{Y'}x_f)\,;\,(x_c^*\theta_{f'})\,;\,(q_xF_{f'})
 = (\widehat B_fq_y)\,;\,(\theta_fG_y)\,;\,(\mathcal R_Xe_f).
$$
Here semicolons mean composition in the displayed order, and adjacent functor/transformation notation denotes whiskering. The equation is before applying $R\lim$ or quotient evaluation. It concerns a single exchange square and has no finite-origin or second compact-support operation.

proof.text: Transpose the ordinary proper projection/exchange square on the single strict quotient diagram. Its adjoints are the same counit tensor the quotient identity, by ringed exchange/tensor coherence. For the open square, transpose the pulled-back open unit; tensor descent sends it to the strict open unit tensored with 1. Pasting these squares gives compatibility of ordinary support reduction with the strict proper-then-open exchange.

proof.text: Use the actual definitions of theta, pullReduction and completedExchange from the ambient comparison node. After strict reduction every inserted completion unit is invertible. Naturality moves these units past the ordinary exchange; invert and cancel them at both endpoints of the ordinary square from the first step. This yields exactly the displayed equality. Identity squares give the unit-normalized identity square; empty opens and zero complexes give the unique zero morphisms. The proof uses neither completeness of inputs nor common lower bounds, and takes no equality from Rlim or evaluations.

lean.statement:
theorem completedExchange_reduction {A : Type (t + 1)} [CommRing A]
    (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) {X U Y X' U' Y' : Scheme.{t}}
    (j : X ⟶ U) (p : U ⟶ Y) (j' : X' ⟶ U') (p' : U' ⟶ Y')
    (x : X' ⟶ X) (u : U' ⟶ U) (y : Y' ⟶ Y)
    [IsOpenImmersion j] [IsOpenImmersion j'] [QuasiCompact j] [QuasiCompact j']
    [IsProper p] [IsProper p'] (hj : x ≫ j = j' ≫ u) (hp : u ≫ p = p' ≫ y)
    (sj : IsPullback x j' j u) (sp : IsPullback u p' p y) :
    whiskerRight (completedExchange d j p j' p' x u y hj hp sj) (reduction d Y') ≫
        whiskerLeft (completePull d x) (theta d j' p') ≫
          whiskerRight (pullReduction d x) (tower (A := A) j' p') =
      whiskerLeft (completed d j p) (pullReduction d y) ≫
        whiskerRight (theta d j p) (G A y) ≫
          whiskerLeft (reduction d X) (strictExchange j p j' p' x u y hj hp sj)
